children.text: tatra kasyacid ekasya vaśe viśvaṃ pravartate |
children.translated_text: The universe operates under the control of some one [being];
in order to establish this, we first set forth the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection).

children.text: tatra kasyacid ekasya vaśe viśvaṃ pravartate |

body.text: tatra mīmāṃsakāḥ prāhuḥ -- nāyaṃ sarvārthadarśanaśaktisampannaḥ puruṣo 'bhyupagamam arhati, atipatitasakalasādhakapramāṇasambhāvanābhūmitvāt sphuṭavividhabādhakatvāc ca / tathā hi -- asya pratyakṣam anyad vā sādhakaṃ bhavet ? pratyakṣam api laukikaṃ yaugikaṃ vā ?
body.translated_text: There the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> say: such a person endowed with the power of perceiving all things cannot be admitted, because the domain of all possible validating <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge) has been exceeded, and because there are manifest and various invalidating considerations. For instance — would the proof of this be <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) or something else? And if perception, would it be ordinary or <s>yaugika</s> (yogic)?

children.text: tatra mīmāṃsakāḥ prāhuḥ --- na ayaṃ sarva-artha-darśana-śakti-sampannaḥ puruṣo 'bhyupagamam arhati, atipatita-sakala-sādhaka-pramāṇa-sambhāvanā-bhūmitvāt sphuṭa-vividha-bādhakatvāc ca / tathā hi --- asya pratyakṣam anyad vā sādhakaṃ bhavet ? pratyakṣam api laukikaṃ yaugikaṃ vā ?

children.translated_text: Ordinary [perception], which is settled, limited, and restricted to its own objects, is certainly not
a proof here, since the omniscience and such [qualities] of that [being] concerning all objects are unestablished.

body.text: sarvārthadarśanaśaktiśālinam avagamayatā hi deśakālasvabhāvaviprakarṣavyavadhānajuṣaḥ sarva evārthās darśanaṃ śaktiś ca gocarayitavyāni / na ca vidyamānendriyasannikarṣayogyakatipayaviṣayaniyatavṛtter laukikapratyakṣasya niravadhir ayaṃ mahimā saṃbhāvanābhūmir iti katham iva tad iha sādhanam iti manyemahi /
body.translated_text: For one who would make known [a being] endowed with the power of perceiving all objects must bring within the range of [that being's] vision and power all objects whatsoever — including those remote in space, time, and nature, or those obstructed. But the limitless glory of ordinary perception, whose operation is restricted to a few objects suitable for contact with the present sense organs, is not within the domain of possibility — so how can we consider it a proof here?

children.text: sarva-artha-darśana-śakti-śālinam avagamayatā hi deśa-kāla-svabhāva-viprakarṣa-vyavadhāna-juṣaḥ sarva eva arthās darśanaṃ śaktiś ca gocarayitavyāni / na ca vidyamāna-indriya-sannikarṣa-yogya-katipaya-viṣaya-niyata-vṛtter laukika-pratyakṣasya niravadhir ayaṃ mahimā saṃbhāvanā-bhūmir iti katham iva tad iha sādhanam iti manyemahi /

body.text: nāpi yogipratyakṣam asya sādhakam; yataḥ --
body.translated_text: Nor is yogic perception a proof of this; because —

children.text: na api yogi-pratyakṣam asya sādhakam; yataḥ ---

children.translated_text: Even that [yogic perception], if it be perceptual, has only presently existing objects as its domain;
it does not perceive past [objects] and such things at all, like <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive flash) and the like.

body.text: tat khalu yogivijñānam aindriyakaṃ na vā ? aindriyakam api bahirindriyasambhavam āntarakaraṇajanitaṃ vā ? bahirindriyāṇi tāvat samadhigatanijaviṣayasannikarṣasahakārīṇi tadgocarajñānajananānīti jagati viditam / ato na rasanādibhir ajātātivṛttavyavahitādisakalaviṣayavedanaprasaṅgaḥ / na cāvidyamānair ajātādibhiḥ saṃbhavati sannikarṣaḥ; tasya hy āśrayatvād āśrayābhāve tadasambhavāt / ato 'pekṣito 'rthasannikarṣaḥ / sahakārivirahe katham indriyāṇy atītādiviṣayasākṣātkārāya kalperan ? / bhavati ca -- yad yatsahakāri yatkāryajananam, tat tadabhāve na taj janayati ; yathā kṣitisalilasahakāri aṅkurakāryajananabījaṃ kṣityādyabhāve 'ṅkuram / arthasannikarṣasahakārīṇi bahirindriyāṇi jñānajananānīti tāny api nātīte 'nāgate vārthe jñānaṃ janayantīti na tad upajanitaṃ pratyakṣaṃ yathoktaviṣayaniyamam atikrāmati /
body.translated_text: Now, is that yogic cognition sense-based or not? If sense-based, does it arise from the external sense organs or from the internal organ? The external sense organs, having acquired contact with their respective objects as an auxiliary condition, generate cognition pertaining to those objects — this is well known in the world. Therefore there is no possibility of the tongue and other [organs] cognizing all objects such as those not yet born, those that have passed away, those that are obstructed, and so on. Nor is there contact possible with non-existing [objects] such as those not yet born, since contact depends on a substratum, and in the absence of the substratum it is impossible. Therefore contact with the object is required. In the absence of auxiliary conditions, how could the sense organs be capable of directly perceiving past and other such objects? And [there is this argument]: whatever generates a certain effect with certain auxiliary conditions does not generate that [effect] in the absence of those [conditions]; just as a seed that generates a sprout with earth and water as auxiliaries [does not produce] a sprout in the absence of earth and the rest. The external sense organs, which generate cognition with contact with objects as an auxiliary, likewise do not generate cognition regarding past or future objects — therefore perception arising from them does not transgress the stated limitation to [present] objects.

children.text: tat khalu yogi-vijñānam aindriyakaṃ na vā ? aindriyakam api bahir-indriya-sambhavam āntara-karaṇa-janitaṃ vā ? bahir-indriyāṇi tāvat samadhigata-nija-viṣaya-sannikarṣa-sahakārīṇi tad-gocara-jñāna-jananāni iti jagati viditam / ato na rasana-ādibhir ajāta-ativṛtta-vyavahita-ādi-sakala-viṣaya-vedana-prasaṅgaḥ / na ca avidyamānair ajāta-ādibhiḥ saṃbhavati sannikarṣaḥ; tasya hy āśrayatvād āśraya-abhāve tad-asambhavāt / ato 'pekṣito 'rtha-sannikarṣaḥ / sahakāri-virahe katham indriyāṇy atīta-ādi-viṣaya-sākṣātkārāya kalperan ? / bhavati ca --- yad yat-sahakāri yat-kārya-jananam, tat tad-abhāve na taj janayati ; yathā kṣiti-salila-sahakāri aṅkura-kārya-janana-bījaṃ kṣity-ādy-abhāve 'ṅkuram / artha-sannikarṣa-sahakārīṇi bahir-indriyāṇi jñāna-jananāni iti tāny api na atīte 'nāgate va ārthe jñānaṃ janayanti iti na tad upajanitaṃ pratyakṣaṃ yathā-ukta-viṣaya-niyamam atikrāmati /

body.text: nāpy antarakaraṇasambhavam, āntaragocara eva sukhādau svāntasvātantryāt / bāhyaviṣayamitiṣu ca manaso niraṅkuśakaraṇatāṅgīkāre hi kṛtaṃ cakṣurādibhiḥ / ataś ca kaścid andho badhiro vā bhavet / bhavati cātra vimatipadaṃ mano bahirindriyanirapekṣaṃ na bāhyapratyakṣagocare pravartate, tatra tattantravṛttitvāt / yady atra yattantravṛtti na tat tannirapekṣaṃ tatra pravartate, yathālokāpekṣapravṛtti cakṣuḥ svagocare 'ndhatamasa iti / na ca siddhāuṣadhamantratapaḥsamādhimahimasamāsāditātiśayānīndriyāṇi kadācid apajahati samadhigataviṣayaniyamam iti sambhavati; sāṃsiddhikasāmārthāvirbhāvaikaphalatvāt teṣām, sāmarthyasya ca pratiniyamāt / na khalu suprayuktabheṣajaśatavihitasaṃskāram api śrotraṃ rūparasavibhāvāvagamāya kalpate / bhavati ca -- vivādādhyāsitabāhyābhyantarakaraṇapāṭavātiśayo 'nullaṅghitasīmā, aindriyakaprakarṣatvāt, dṛśyamānatatprakarṣavad ity aindriyakaṃ jñānaṃ nātītādi gocarayati /
body.translated_text: Nor does [yogic cognition] arise from the internal organ, for the internal [organ] operates independently only with respect to internal objects such as pleasure and the like. If the unrestricted agency of the mind with respect to external objects and their cognition were accepted, then the eyes and other [organs] would be rendered purposeless. And then someone would be blind or deaf [for no reason]. And here the debatable point is this: the mind, without dependence on the external sense organs, does not operate in the domain of external perception, because its functioning there depends on those [external organs]. If that which depends on something for its functioning does not operate there without that [dependency], just as the eye, whose functioning depends on light, [does not operate] in its own domain in complete darkness. Nor is it possible that the sense organs, having acquired extraordinary powers through the efficacy of <s>siddha</s>-substances, medicines, <s>mantras</s>, <s>tapas</s> (austerities), and <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), sometimes abandon their established limitation to [specific] objects; for these [enhancements] have as their sole result the manifestation of innate capacities, and those capacities are each specifically delimited. Surely the ear, even when refined by hundreds of well-applied medicines, is not capable of apprehending forms and tastes. And [there is this argument]: the extraordinary refinement of the external and internal organs under dispute does not transgress its limits, because it is a refinement of sense-based [cognition], just as observed refinements of those [organs] [do not transgress their limits] — therefore sense-based cognition does not have past and other [objects] as its domain.

children.text: na apy antarakaraṇa-sambhavam, āntaragocara eva sukha-ādau sva-anta-svātantryāt / bāhya-viṣaya-mitiṣu ca manaso niraṅkuśa-karaṇatā-aṅgīkāre hi kṛtaṃ cakṣur-ādibhiḥ / ataś ca kaścid andho badhiro vā bhavet / bhavati ca atra vimati-padaṃ mano bahir-indriya-nirapekṣaṃ na bāhya-pratyakṣa-gocare pravartate, tatra tat-tantra-vṛttitvāt / yady atra yat-tantra-vṛtti na tat tan-nirapekṣaṃ tatra pravartate, yathā āloka-apekṣa-pravṛtti cakṣuḥ sva-gocare 'ndha-tamasa iti / na ca siddha-auṣadha-mantra-tapaḥ-samādhi-mahima-samāsādita-atiśayāni indriyāṇi kadācid apajahati samadhigata-viṣaya-niyamam iti sambhavati; sāṃsiddhika-sāmārtha-āvirbhāva-eka-phalatvāt teṣām, sāmarthyasya ca pratiniyamāt / na khalu suprayukta-bheṣa-ja-śata-vihita-saṃskāram api śrotraṃ rūpa-rasa-vibhāva-avagamāya kalpate / bhavati ca --- vivāda-adhyāsita-bāhya-abhyantara-karaṇa-pāṭava-atiśayo 'nullaṅghita-sīmā, aindriyaka-prakarṣatvāt, dṛśyamāna-tat-prakarṣavad ity aindriyakaṃ jñānaṃ na atīta-ādi gocarayati /

body.text: bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajanmanas tu saty api viśadanirbhāsatve prācyānubhavagocarād anadhikam adhikaṃ vādhyavasyataḥ smṛtivibhramasrotasor anyatarāvartaparivartinaḥ kutaḥ prāmāṇyakūlapratilabhaḥ ? kutastarāṃ ca pratyakṣatayottambhanam ? / pratyakṣasya vā sataḥ katham iva viditaviṣayaniyamavyatikramaḥ ? atikrāmato vā kutaḥ pratyakṣatvam iti na viśvānubhavāiśvaryaśālini pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam /
body.translated_text: But as for [cognition] born at the culmination of meditative cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — even though it possesses vivid manifestation, [since] it determines either no more than, or even more than, the domain of prior experience, [and since] it revolves in one or the other of the two currents of memory (<s>smṛti</s>) and delusion (<s>vibhrama</s>) — how could it attain the shore of valid authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>)? And how, even more, could it be propped up as direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>)? Or if it were direct perception, how could it transgress the fixed boundaries of [its own] known domain? And if it does transgress, how could it be direct perception? Therefore, direct perception is not a valid means of knowledge for one who claims lordship over universal experience.

children.text: bhāvanā-prakarṣa-paryanta-janmanas tu saty api viśada-nirbhāsatve prācya-anubhava-gocarād anadhikam adhikaṃ va ādhyavasyataḥ smṛti-vibhrama-srotasor anyatara-āvarta-parivartinaḥ kutaḥ prāmāṇya-kūla-pratilabhaḥ ? kutastarāṃ ca pratyakṣataya ūttambhanam ? / pratyakṣasya vā sataḥ katham iva vidita-viṣaya-niyama-vyatikramaḥ ? atikrāmato vā kutaḥ pratyakṣatvam iti na viśva-anubhava-aiśvarya-śālini pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam /

body.text: nāpi pramāṇāntaram / tat khalv anumānam āgamo vā ? anumānam api viśeṣato dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ vā ? tatra sakalapadavīdavīyasi bhavati na tāvat svalakṣaṇasākṣātkārapūrvakāvinābhāvāvadhāraṇādhīnodayatvād idam anumānam udetum alam / na hy anavagatacarahutabhujas tadavinābhāvitayā dhūmam anusandhātum īśate / na ca sarvārthanirmāṇasākṣātkārapaṭīyasi liṅgaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭam api kiñcana labhate /
body.translated_text: Nor is there another means of valid knowledge [for this purpose]. Is that [other means] inference (<s>anumāna</s>) or scripture (<s>āgama</s>)? And is the inference based on a particular observation (<s>viśeṣato dṛṣṭa</s>) or on a general observation (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>)? In that [case], when [the object in question] courses beyond all [ordinary] paths: first, this inference, whose arising depends on the ascertainment of invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) preceded by the direct perception of the particular characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), is not capable of arising. For one who has not apprehended [even the nature of] fire in motion cannot investigate smoke as being invariably concomitant with it. Nor, for one who is proficient in the direct perception of the production of all objects, is any inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) — even one based on general observation — [needed or] obtained.

children.text: na api pramāṇa-antaram / tat khalv anumānam āgamo vā ? anumānam api viśeṣato dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ vā ? tatra sakala-padavī-davīyasi bhavati na tāvat sva-lakṣaṇa-sākṣātkāra-pūrvaka-avinābhāva-avadhāraṇa-adhīna-udayatvād idam anumānam udetum alam / na hy anavagata-cara-huta-bhujas tad-avinābhāvitayā dhūmam anusandhātum īśate / na ca sarva-artha-nirmāṇa-sākṣātkāra-paṭīyasi liṅgaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭam api kiñcana labhate /

children.translated_text: [Argument:] The disputed world is dependent on a single conscious being,
because it is not produced by something non-conscious — like one's own healthy body.
Likewise, proficiency in the direct perception of the production of all objects
should be inferred of the maker of the world, precisely because of [its] being an effect (<s>kārya</s>).

body.text: sarvaṃ hi kāryam upādānopakaraṇasampradānaprayojanasaṃvedicetanaracitam avagataṃ ghaṭamaṇikagṛhādi / kāryaṃ ca vimatipadam avanigirimahārṇavādīti tad api tathāvidhabuddhimaddhetukam adhyavasīyate / na ca kāryatvam asiddham iti vācyam, avayavasanniveśādibhir hetubhis tatsiddheḥ / iha cānyāvayavibhyaḥ prabhṛti ādvyaṇukam akhilam avayavi kramanihīyamānanānāvayavavyatiṣaṅgaviśeṣajanitam avagatam ity antata upādānaṃ caturvidhāḥ paramāṇavaḥ prapañcasya / teṣām ādiparispandasya tadanuguṇādṛṣṭaviśiṣṭatattatkṣetrajñasaṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇaka iti upakaraṇam api samastakṣetrajñavartini dharmādharmalakṣaṇāny adṛṣṭāni / prayojanaṃ punastadabhinirvartitavicitrārthakriyākāraś cetanopakārapakārabhedo 'payantaḥ / tadupabhujasta eva kṣetrajñāḥ sampradānam / na cāmī svasamavāyināv api dharmādharmāvalam avalokayitum iti tadatirekī nikhilabhuvananirmāṇanipuṇo 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntasamadhigataniratiśayasahajasakalaviṣayasaṃvidaiśvaryaśaktyatiśayaḥ puruṣadhaureyakaḥ kim iti na sāmānyatodṛṣṭaliṅgād anumīyate ?
body.translated_text: For every effect is observed to be produced by a conscious being who is aware of the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), instrument (<s>upakaraṇa</s>), recipient (<s>sampradāna</s>), and purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) — such as pots, jeweled necklaces, houses, and the like. And the subject of dispute — the earth, mountains, great oceans, and the rest — being effects, they too are to be determined as having an intelligent cause of that very kind. Nor should it be said that [their] being effects is unestablished, since that is established by reasons such as the arrangement of parts (<s>avayavasanniveśa</s>) and the like. Here, moreover, every composite entity (<s>avayavin</s>), from things composed of atoms other [than itself] up to the dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>), is understood to be produced by the specific conjunction of its progressively diminishing various parts — so ultimately, the material cause of the manifest world is the four kinds of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>). Their initial vibration (<s>ādiparispanda</s>) has as its non-inherence cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>) the conjunction of each individual soul (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) possessing unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) appropriate to that [initial motion]. And the instrument (<s>upakaraṇa</s>) is the unseen [forces] characterized as <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), residing in all individual souls. The purpose, moreover, is the [consequent] variety of beneficial and harmful effects produced [for] conscious beings, terminating in the variety of useful functions. The individual souls themselves, who enjoy those [effects], are the recipients (<s>sampradāna</s>). And since these [souls] are not capable of seeing even the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> inherent in themselves — why should not a Person supreme (<s>puruṣadhaureyaka</s>), distinct from them, skilled in the construction of the entire universe, possessing a supremacy of power [characterized by] the lordship of innate cognition of all objects without limit — established by the principle of the substrate — be inferred through an inferential mark based on general observation?

children.text: sarvaṃ hi kāryam upādāna-upakaraṇa-sampradāna-prayojana-saṃvedi-cetana-racitam avagataṃ ghaṭa-maṇika-gṛha-ādi / kāryaṃ ca vimati-padam avani-giri-mahā-arṇava-ādi iti tad api tathā-vidha-buddhimad-dhetukam adhyavasīyate / na ca kāryatvam asiddham iti vācyam, avayava-sanniveśa-ādibhir hetubhis tat-siddheḥ / iha ca anya-avayavibhyaḥ prabhṛti ā-dvyaṇukam akhilam avayavi krama-nihīyamāna-nānā-avayava-vyatiṣaṅga-viśeṣa-janitam avagatam ity antata upādānaṃ catur-vidhāḥ parama-aṇavaḥ prapañcasya / teṣām ādi-parispandasya tad-anuguṇa-adṛṣṭa-viśiṣṭa-tat-tat-kṣetra-jña-saṃyoga-asamavāyikāraṇaka iti upakaraṇam api samasta-kṣetra-jña-vartini dharma-adharma-lakṣaṇāny adṛṣṭāni / prayojanaṃ punas-tad-abhinirvartita-vicitra-artha-kriyā-kāraś cetana-upakāra-pakāra-bhedo 'payantaḥ / tad-upabhujasta eva kṣetra-jñāḥ sampradānam / na ca amī sva-samavāyināv api dharma-adharma-avalam avalokayitum iti tad-atirekī nikhila-bhuvana-nirmāṇa-nipuṇo 'dhikaraṇa-siddhānta-samadhigata-niratiśaya-sahaja-sakala-viṣaya-saṃvid-aiśvarya-śakty-atiśayaḥ puruṣa-dhaureyakaḥ kim iti na sāmānyato-dṛṣṭa-liṅgād anumīyate ?

body.text: tad idam aviditānumānavṛttasya svamatiracitataralatarkollasitam iti parihasanti mīmāṃsakāḥ / tathā hi -- kim idam ekacetanādhīnatvaṃ nāmābhipretaṃ tanubhuvanādeḥ ? / tadāyattatvam iti cet;
body.translated_text: The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> ridicule this [argument] as a display of fickle reasoning concocted by one's own intellect, by one who is ignorant of the actual procedure of inference. For thus [they object]: What is this 'dependence on a single conscious being' that is intended with respect to the body, the world, and so forth? If [you mean] dependence (<s>āyattatva</s>) on that [single being] —

children.text: tad idam avidita-anumāna-vṛttasya sva-mati-racita-tarala-tarka-ullasitam iti parihasanti mīmāṃsakāḥ / tathā hi --- kim idam eka-cetana-adhīnatvaṃ nāma abhipretaṃ tanu-bhuvana-ādeḥ ? / tad-āyattatvam iti cet;
kim asya tasminn āyattaṃ kiṃ nu janmātha vā sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: What of this [world] depends on that [being]? Is it its origination or its continued existence?
Or its activity? — As for the first two, the example is devoid of the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).

children.text: kim asya tasminn āyattaṃ kiṃ nu janma atha vā sthitiḥ |
pravṛttir vā ādyayos tāvat sādhya-hīnaṃ nidarśanam ||

body.text: na khalu śarīram ekacetanādhīnotpattisthiti / ye hi yaddehādhīnasukhaduḥkhopabhogabhāginaḥ, bhavati hi taducitādṛṣṭaśālināṃ sarveṣām eva teṣāṃ taddehina iva tadutpattisthitinimittatvam / api ca śarīrāvayavinaḥ svāvayavasamavāyalakṣaṇā sthitir avayavyatiṣaṅgaviśeṣād ṛte na cetayitāraṃ param apekṣate / yā punas tadapekṣiṇī prāṇanalakṣaṇā sthitiḥ, na sā pakṣīkṛte kṣityādau sambhavatīti sthitim api naikarūpāṃ pakṣasapakṣānuyāyinīm udīkṣāmahe / ekacetanādhīnapravṛttitve tu prabalabahujanasarabhasaprayatnapracālyair upalatarurathādibhir vyabhicāraḥ / ārabdhatvād eva caitatsādhyasiddhābadhikam idam upādānaviśeṣavacanam /
body.translated_text: The body is certainly not [something] whose origination and continued existence depend on a single conscious being. For all those who share in the experience of pleasure and pain dependent on a given body — since all of them possess unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) appropriate to that [body], just like the embodied soul [itself] — have the status of being the cause of that [body's] origination and continued existence. Moreover, the continued existence of the bodily composite entity — characterized by the inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) of its own parts — does not, apart from the specific conjunction of parts, require a further conscious being. And that continued existence which does require [a conscious being], characterized by life-breath (<s>prāṇana</s>), is not possible in the thesis-object (<s>pakṣa</s>), namely earth and the like. Therefore we do not see a continued existence of a single nature that uniformly follows both the thesis and the positive instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>). As for dependence on a single conscious being for activity — there is deviation [from the rule], since stones, trees, chariots, and the like are moved by the vigorous efforts of many powerful persons. And this statement specifying a [particular type of] material cause is [mere] restatement of [what is already] established through [the property] of being produced — hence it does not go beyond [what is already established as] the property to be proved.

children.text: na khalu śarīram eka-cetana-adhīna-utpatti-sthiti / ye hi yad-deha-adhīna-sukha-duḥkha-upabhoga-bhāginaḥ, bhavati hi tad-ucita-adṛṣṭa-śālināṃ sarveṣām eva teṣāṃ tad-dehina iva tad-utpatti-sthiti-nimittatvam / api ca śarīra-avayavinaḥ sva-avayava-samavāya-lakṣaṇā sthitir avayavy-atiṣaṅga-viśeṣād ṛte na cetayitāraṃ param apekṣate / yā punas tad-apekṣiṇī prāṇana-lakṣaṇā sthitiḥ, na sā pakṣīkṛte kṣity-ādau sambhavati iti sthitim api na eka-rūpāṃ pakṣa-sapakṣa-anuyāyinīm udīkṣāmahe / eka-cetana-adhīna-pravṛttitve tu prabala-bahu-jana-sarabhasa-prayatna-pracālyair upala-taru-ratha-ādibhir vyabhicāraḥ / ārabdhatvād eva ca etat-sādhya-siddha-abadhikam idam upādāna-viśeṣa-vacanam /

children.translated_text: In proving mere dependence on a conscious being, there is the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>);

children.text: cetanair bhoktṛbhir bhogyaḥ karmabhir janyate hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: for according to us, the world, being [an object] to be enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>), is produced by <s>karmas</s> (actions) for conscious enjoyers (<s>bhoktṛ</s>).

children.text: cetanair bhoktṛbhir bhogyaḥ karmabhir janyate hi naḥ ||

body.text: yuktaṃ caitat -- yadubhayavādisiddhānām eva cetanānāṃ kartṛtvābhyupagamaḥ; lāghavāt / na copādānādyanabhijñatayā tatpratikṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: And this is reasonable — that the acceptance of agency belongs to conscious beings alone, which are established by both parties [in the debate]; because of simplicity (<s>lāghava</s>). Nor is there a rejection of that [agency] due to unfamiliarity with the material cause and other [factors].

children.text: yuktaṃ ca etat --- yad-ubhaya-vādi-siddhānām eva cetanānāṃ kartṛtva-abhyupagamaḥ; lāghavāt / na ca upādāna-ādy-anabhijñatayā tat-pratikṣepaḥ /

children.translated_text: The material cause is earth and such; the means is sacrifice, gift-giving, and such;

children.text: sākṣātkartuṃ kṣamante yat sarva eva ca cetanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all conscious beings indeed are capable of directly perceiving [these].

children.text: sākṣātkartuṃ kṣamante yat sarva eva ca cetanāḥ ||

body.text: adyavad eva viśvambharādayaḥ kramaprāptāgantukopacayāpacayaikadeśaśālino na yugapad eva niravaśeṣavilayajananabhāgina ityantimaparamāṇusākṣātkāro na kartṛbhāvopayogī /
body.translated_text: The earth-bearer and such, just as at present, possess portions of gradually-acquired adventitious increase and decrease, and are not subject to simultaneous complete dissolution and generation — therefore the direct perception of the ultimate atom is not useful for [establishing] agency.

children.text: adyavad eva viśvambhara-ādayaḥ krama-prāpta-āgantuka-upacaya-apacaya-eka-deśa-śālino na yugapad eva niravaśeṣa-vilaya-janana-bhāgina ity-antima-parama-aṇu-sākṣātkāro na kartṛ-bhāva-upayogī /

children.translated_text: That which is the form of power (<s>śakti</s>) of <s>karma</s> (action), which is the locus of prior [causal] states —

children.text: mā bhūt pratyakṣatā tasya śaktimad dhy akṣagocaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: let there be no direct perceptibility of that; for what possesses power is indeed within the range of the senses.

children.text: mā bhūt pratyakṣatā tasya śaktimad dhy akṣa-gocaraḥ ||

body.text: na khalu kulālādayaḥ kumbhādikāryam ārabhamāṇās tadupādānopakaraṇabhūtamṛddaṇḍacakrādikāryotpādanaśaktiṃ sākṣātkṛtya tat tad ārabhante / yadi paraṃ śaktim aviduṣām abhilaṣitasādhane tadupādānādivyavahāro 'nupapannaḥ, iha tu --
body.translated_text: Surely, potters and such, when producing effects like pots, do not first directly perceive the power to produce effects in the material cause, instruments, and accessories such as clay, stick, wheel, and so on, and then undertake those [productions]. If, however, the engagement with material causes and such for accomplishing what is desired is impossible for those who do not know the power, then here —

children.text: na khalu kulāla-ādayaḥ kumbha-ādi-kāryam ārabhamāṇās tad-upādāna-upakaraṇa-bhūta-mṛd-daṇḍa-cakra-ādi-kārya-utpādana-śaktiṃ sākṣātkṛtya tat tad ārabhante / yadi paraṃ śaktim aviduṣām abhilaṣita-sādhane tad-upādāna-ādi-vyavahāro 'nupapannaḥ, iha tu ---

children.translated_text: The various powers of <s>karma</s> (action) are understood from scripture (<s>āgama</s>);

children.text: tena karmabhir ātmānaḥ sarvaṃ nirmimatāṃ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: therefore, through actions, let individual selves (<s>ātman</s>) each create everything.

children.text: tena karmabhir ātmānaḥ sarvaṃ nirmimatāṃ pṛthak ||

body.text: api ca tad eva cetanakarṭrkaṃ jagati paridṛśyate, yad eva śakyakriyaṃ śakyajñānopādānādi ca / na ca tathā mahīmahīśvaramahārṇavādīti katham iva tattatkāryatvam ? kathantarāṃ ca tadupādānopakaraṇādeḥ sākṣātkāragocaratā ? yādṛśaṃ hi kāryam upādānādyabhijñapūrvakam avagataṃ ghaṭamaṇikādi, tādṛśam eva hi tathāvidhabuddhimaddhetukatvānumānāya prabhavati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, precisely that is observed in the world as having a conscious agent, which is capable of being produced, and whose material cause and such are capable of being known. But the earth, the lord of the earth (mountains), the great ocean, and such are not so — how then can they be effects of [a limited agent]? And how can their material cause, instruments, and such be within the range of direct perception? For only such effects as are understood to be preceded by knowledge of their material cause and such — pots, jewels, and the like — can serve as the basis for inferring a cause possessing such knowledge.

children.text: api ca tad eva cetana-karṭrkaṃ jagati paridṛśyate, yad eva śakya-kriyaṃ śakya-jñāna-upādāna-ādi ca / na ca tathā mahī-mahīśvara-mahārṇava-ādi iti katham iva tat-tat-kāryatvam ? kathantarāṃ ca tad-upādāna-upakaraṇa-ādeḥ sākṣātkāra-gocaratā ? yādṛśaṃ hi kāryam upādāna-ādy-abhijña-pūrvakam avagataṃ ghaṭa-maṇika-ādi, tādṛśam eva hi tathā-vidha-buddhimad-dhetukatva-anumānāya prabhavati /

body.text: api cānīśvareṇa parimitaśaktijñānena vigrahavatānavāptakāmena kṛtam avagataṃ ghaṭādikāryam iti tathāvidhaṃ boddhāram upasthāpayan hetur abhimatapuruṣasārvajñyasarvāiśvaryādiviparyayasādhanādiviruddhaḥ syāt / na caivaṃ sati sarvānumānavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgaḥ śaṅkitavyaḥ / pramāṇāntaragocare hi liṅgini liṅgabalād āpatato viparītaviśeṣāṃs tatpramāṇam eva pratiruṇaddhi / iha punar atipatitasakalamānāntarakarmabhāve sarvanirmāṇanipuṇe siṣādhayiṣite yāvanto 'nvayavyatirekāvadhāritāvinābhāvabhājo dharmās tān apy aviśeṣeṇopasthāpayati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, pots and such effects are understood to have been produced by a non-omnipotent [agent] of limited power and knowledge, who has a body and whose desires are unfulfilled — a reason (<s>hetu</s>) that presents such a knower would be contradictory, proving the opposite of the desired [conclusion regarding God's] omniscience, supreme sovereignty, and so on. Nor should it be suspected that in this case there would be the unwanted consequence of the destruction of all inferential reasoning. For when the inferendum (<s>liṅgin</s>) is within the domain of another means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), that very means of knowledge blocks the specific contrary [attributes] that would accrue from the force of the inferential mark alone. But here, when what is to be proved is [a being] who, being beyond the range of all other means of knowledge, is skilled in creating everything — all the properties whose invariable concomitance has been ascertained through agreement and difference are presented without any distinction.

children.text: api ca anīśvareṇa parimita-śakti-jñānena vigrahavata ānavāpta-kāmena kṛtam avagataṃ ghaṭa-ādi-kāryam iti tathā-vidhaṃ boddhāram upasthāpayan hetur abhimata-puruṣa-sārvajñya-sarva-aiśvarya-ādi-viparyaya-sādhana-ādi-viruddhaḥ syāt / na ca evaṃ sati sarva-anumāna-vyavahāra-uccheda-prasaṅgaḥ śaṅkitavyaḥ / pramāṇa-antara-gocare hi liṅgini liṅga-balād āpatato viparīta-viśeṣāṃs tat-pramāṇam eva pratiruṇaddhi / iha punar atipatita-sakala-māna-antara-karma-bhāve sarva-nirmāṇa-nipuṇe siṣādhayiṣite yāvanto 'nvaya-vyatireka-avadhāritā-avinā-bhāva-bhājo dharmās tān apy aviśeṣeṇa upasthāpayati /

body.text: api ca --
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: The actions of a deliberate agent are pervaded by [either] self-interest or compassion;
for God (<s>Īśvara</s>), since both are absent, the creation of the world is not justified.

body.text: avāptakāmatvān na tāvad ātmārthe sṛjati; pralayasamaye pralīnasakalakaraṇakalevarādibhogopakaraṇatayā ca cetanānāṃ duḥkhābhāvād duḥkhidarśanajanitakṛpāprayuktir api nāstīti vyāpakabhūtasvārthakāruṇyanivṛtter vyāpyabhūtayā prekṣāvatpravṛttyāpi nivartitavyam /
body.translated_text: Since His desires are fulfilled (<s>avāptakāma</s>), He does not create for His own sake; and since at the time of dissolution, when all instruments of enjoyment such as bodies, sense-organs, and the like of conscious beings have dissolved, there is no suffering [for them], the motivation arising from compassion produced by seeing the suffering [of beings] also does not exist — therefore, since the pervading [properties] of self-interest and compassion have ceased, the pervaded [property], namely deliberate activity, must also be negated.

children.text: avāpta-kāmatvān na tāvad ātma-arthe sṛjati; pralaya-samaye pralīna-sakala-karaṇa-kalevara-ādi-bhoga-upakaraṇatayā ca cetanānāṃ duḥkha-abhāvād duḥkhi-darśana-janita-kṛpā-prayuktir api na asti iti vyāpaka-bhūta-sva-artha-kāruṇya-nivṛtter vyāpya-bhūtayā prekṣāvat-pravṛttya āpi nivartitavyam /

children.translated_text: [Objection:] Creating out of compassion, He should produce a world consisting entirely of happiness;
[but] if He [merely] conforms to the <s>karma</s> of those [beings], His independence (<s>svatantratā</s>) would be diminished.

body.text: na copādānādisākṣātkāriṇi eva kartṛtvam ity api niyamaḥ; upādānam upakaraṇaṃ cāviduṣa evātmano jñānādiṣu kartṛtvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there a rule that agency belongs only to one who directly perceives the material cause and such; for the self (<s>ātman</s>), even without knowing [its own material cause], has agency with respect to cognition and the like.

children.text: na ca upādāna-ādi-sākṣātkāriṇi eva kartṛtvam ity api niyamaḥ; upādānam upakaraṇaṃ ca aviduṣa evā atmano jñāna-ādiṣu kartṛtvāt /

body.text: ataḥ --
body.translated_text: Therefore:

children.translated_text: Because of being unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), because of being contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and because of the described inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntya</s>),
the world does not have agency as described, [merely] from the reason of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>).

body.text: prayogaś ca bhavati -- mahīmahīdharādi kāryaṃ na bhavati, prasiddhakāryavilakṣaṇatvāt, gaganavat; aśakyadarśanopādānopakaraṇatvād vā, vyatirekeṇa ghaṭādivat / paramāṇavo na pratyakṣāḥ niratiśayasūkṣmadravyatvāt, tathaiva ghaṭādivat / vimativiṣayaḥ kāle na lokaśūnyaḥ, kālatvād idānīntanakālavat / tanubhuvanādīśvarakartṛkaṃ na bhavati kāryatvāt tadvad eva / īśvaraḥ kartā na bhavati prayojanarahitatvād aśarīratvād vā muktātmavad iti /
body.translated_text: And the [opponent's] formal arguments are: The earth, mountains, and such are not effects, because they differ from well-known effects, like space; or because their material cause, instruments, and such cannot be observed, unlike pots and such, by negative concomitance. Atoms are not perceptible, because they are substances of unsurpassable subtlety, just like [the atoms of] pots and such. The subject of doubt — time — is not devoid of the world, because it is time, like present time. The body, the world, and such are not made by God (<s>Īśvara</s>), because they are effects, just like those [pots and such]. God is not an agent because He lacks a motive, or because He is bodiless, like a liberated soul.

children.text: prayogaś ca bhavati --- mahī-mahīdhara-ādi kāryaṃ na bhavati, prasiddha-kārya-vilakṣaṇatvāt, gaganavat; aśakya-darśana-upādāna-upakaraṇatvād vā, vyatirekeṇa ghaṭa-ādivat / parama-aṇavo na pratyakṣāḥ niratiśaya-sūkṣma-dravyatvāt, tatha aiva ghaṭa-ādivat / vimati-viṣayaḥ kāle na loka-śūnyaḥ, kālatvād idānīntana-kālavat / tanu-bhuvana-ādi-īśvara-kartṛkaṃ na bhavati kāryatvāt tadvad eva / īśvaraḥ kartā na bhavati prayojana-rahitatvād aśarīratvād vā mukta-ātmavad iti /
atra brūmo na kāryatvaṃ kṣityādau śakyanihnavam |
children.translated_text: Here we say: the effectness (<s>kāryatva</s>) of the earth and such cannot be denied,
because of having parts (<s>sabhāgatva</s>), because of possessing activity, and especially because of [their] magnitude;

children.text: atra brūmo na kāryatvaṃ kṣity-ādau śakya-nihnavam |

children.translated_text: because of corporeality of precisely such a kind, accompanied by external perceptibility;
and because of possessing both universals and particulars — and so on — just like pots and such.

body.text: na cedṛśa eva sanniveśaḥ kāryaḥ, netara ity avayavasanniveśaviśeṣapratiniyataṃ rūpabhedam udīkṣāmahe / yat tu śakyakriyaṃ śakyajñānopādānopakaraṇaṃ ca kriyata iti, tad astu nāma / kin tu te kriyājñānaśaktī kriyājñānābhyām eva samadhigamanīye / te ca kṣityādiṣu yathoktasādhanabalasamupasthāpite iti na viśeṣaḥ prasiddhaprākāragopurādikāryebhyas tanubhuvanādeḥ / na caitāvān eva kriyāgocara iti viṣayaniyamaḥ kaścit kriyāyā dṛṣṭaḥ; yenedam aśakyakriyam adhyavasyema / siddhe ca kāryatve tadupādānādisakṣātkaraṇatadadhiṣṭhānatatpreraṇanipuṇaḥ puruṣaviśeṣaḥ sidhyaty eva /
body.translated_text: It is not the case that only this particular arrangement [of parts] should be the effect and no other — [yet] we observe that different forms are invariably determined by specific arrangements of constituent parts. As for the argument that what can be acted upon and what requires skill, knowledge, and instruments of production is [indeed] produced — let that be so. But those capacities for action and knowledge are to be ascertained precisely through action and knowledge [themselves]. And these, in [the case of elements like] earth and the rest, are brought about by the force of the means described above — so there is no difference between bodies, worlds, and the like and well-known effects such as city-walls, gate-towers, and the like. And no restriction of scope for action has been observed [to the effect that] 'only this much is the domain of action' — by which we would conclude that this [universe] is incapable of being produced. And when the effect-nature [of the world] is established, a special person (<s>puruṣaviśeṣa</s>) who is skilled in directly perceiving its material cause and the rest, in superintending them, and in directing them, is necessarily established.

children.text: na cā idṛśa eva sanniveśaḥ kāryaḥ, na itara ity avayava-sanniveśa-viśeṣa-pratiniyataṃ rūpa-bhedam udīkṣāmahe / yat tu śakya-kriyaṃ śakya-jñāna-upādāna-upakaraṇaṃ ca kriyata iti, tad astu nāma / kin tu te kriyā-jñāna-śaktī kriyā-jñānābhyām eva samadhigamanīye / te ca kṣity-ādiṣu yathā-ukta-sādhana-bala-samupasthāpite iti na viśeṣaḥ prasiddha-prākāra-gopura-ādi-kāryebhyas tanu-bhuvana-ādeḥ / na ca etāvān eva kriyā-gocara iti viṣaya-niyamaḥ kaścit kriyāyā dṛṣṭaḥ; yena idam aśakya-kriyam adhyavasyema / siddhe ca kāryatve tad-upādāna-ādi-sakṣātkaraṇa-tad-adhiṣṭhāna-tat-preraṇa-nipuṇaḥ puruṣa-viśeṣaḥ sidhyaty eva /

body.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca tatpravṛttyanuguṇasaṅkalpavadīśvarasannikarṣaḥ, kṣetrajñeneva svaśarīrādau / sa ca dravyaiḥ saṃyogalakṣaṇaḥ, tadguṇais tu saṃyuktasamavāyarūpaḥ / pravṛttiś ca paramāṇūnāṃ parispandalakṣaṇā; dharmādharmayos tu phalodayānukūlatādṛśadeśakālādisahakārisahitatā / tābhyāṃ dharmādharmābhyām eva phalam, cetanānadhiṣṭhitānāṃ sarveṣām eteṣām acaitanyenākiñcitkaratvāt / na hi cetanena vardhakinānadhiṣṭhitā vāsī deśakālādisahakāriśatasamadhigame 'pi yūpādīny upādayitum alam / bījāṅkurādayas tu pakṣāntarbhūtā iti tair vyabhicāravacanam anabhijñatayaiva śrotriyāṇām / etena sukhādibhir vyabhicāro 'pi pratyuktaḥ / na cobhayavādisiddhatāmātreṇa kṣetrajñānām evedṛśādhiṣṭhātṛtvakalpanam ucitam; teṣāṃ sūkṣmavyavahitādidarśanāśakter niścitatvāt / dṛṣṭānusāriṇī hi sarvatra kalpanā; na dṛṣṭavirodhinī / na caivam īśvarasyāśaktir niścitā; pramāṇāntaratas tatsiddheḥ / yathoditapramāṇabalena sidhyan sāṃsiddhikasarvārthadarśanatatpreraṇaśaktisampanna eva sidhyati; kāryatvasya samarthakartṛpūrvakatvena pratibandhāt /
body.translated_text: Superintendence (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) is the proximity of <s>Īśvara</s> (God), who possesses a volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) conforming to [the world's] activity — just as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (embodied soul) [superintends] its own body and the like. And that [proximity] with substances is of the nature of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>); with their qualities, it is of the nature of inherence-in-what-is-conjoined (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>). And the activity of the atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) is characterized by vibration (<s>parispanda</s>); but for <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), [their activity consists in] being accompanied by cooperating conditions of appropriate place, time, and the like that are favorable to the ripening of [their] fruit. From those two — <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> alone — comes the fruit, since all these [other factors], when not superintended by a conscious being (<s>cetana</s>), are utterly ineffective due to their unconsciousness. For indeed, an adze not superintended by a conscious carpenter is not capable of producing a sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) and the like, even when hundreds of cooperating conditions of place, time, and the rest are present. Seeds, sprouts, and the like, however, are included within [our] thesis — so citing them as counter-examples [is made] only through the ignorance of those learned in scripture. By this, the counter-example of pleasure and the like is also answered. Nor is it appropriate to imagine that the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (individual souls) alone have such superintending power, merely because they are accepted by both parties [in the debate] — since their incapacity to perceive subtle, obstructed, and similar [objects] is established. For conceptual construction everywhere follows what is observed, not what contradicts observation. And the incapacity of <s>Īśvara</s> has not been thus established — since His existence is proved by other <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge). [The being] that is proved by the force of the <s>pramāṇas</s> stated above is established as endowed with innate powers of perceiving all objects and directing them — because effect-nature is invariably preceded by a competent agent.

children.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca tat-pravṛtty-anuguṇa-saṅkalpavad-īśvara-sannikarṣaḥ, kṣetra-jñena iva sva-śarīra-ādau / sa ca dravyaiḥ saṃyoga-lakṣaṇaḥ, tad-guṇais tu saṃyukta-samavāya-rūpaḥ / pravṛttiś ca parama-aṇūnāṃ parispanda-lakṣaṇā; dharma-adharmayos tu phala-udaya-anukūla-tādṛśa-deśa-kāla-ādi-sahakāri-sahitatā / tābhyāṃ dharma-adharmābhyām eva phalam, cetana-anadhiṣṭhitānāṃ sarveṣām eteṣām acaitanyena akiñcitkaratvāt / na hi cetanena vardhakina ānadhiṣṭhitā vāsī deśa-kāla-ādi-sahakāri-śata-samadhigame 'pi yūpa-ādīny upādayitum alam / bīja-aṅkura-ādayas tu pakṣa-antarbhūtā iti tair vyabhicāra-vacanam anabhijñataya aiva śrotriyāṇām / etena sukha-ādibhir vyabhicāro 'pi pratyuktaḥ / na ca ubhaya-vādi-siddhatā-mātreṇa kṣetra-jñānām evā idṛśa-adhiṣṭhātṛtva-kalpanam ucitam; teṣāṃ sūkṣma-vyavahita-ādi-darśana-aśakter niścitatvāt / dṛṣṭa-anusāriṇī hi sarvatra kalpanā; na dṛṣṭa-virodhinī / na ca evam īśvarasya aśaktir niścitā; pramāṇa-antaratas tat-siddheḥ / yathā-udita-pramāṇa-balena sidhyan sāṃsiddhika-sarva-artha-darśana-tat-preraṇa-śakti-sampanna eva sidhyati; kāryatvasya samartha-kartṛ-pūrvakatvena pratibandhāt /

body.text: yat tu parimitaśaktijñānānaiśvaryādyāpādanād dharmaviśeṣaviparītasādhanatvam udbhāvitam, tad atisthavīyaḥ, aprayojakatvāt teṣām / na hi kiñcit kriyamāṇaṃ kartur arthāntaraviṣayam asāmarthyam ajñānaṃ vā svotpattaye 'pekṣate; svasampādanasamarthakartṛmātrākṣepāt kevalavyatirekāsiddheḥ / tāvataivopapadyamāne kāryodaye sambandhino 'kiñcitkarasyārthāntaraviṣayasyābhāvasya hetutvakalpanānupapatteḥ / api ca kiṃ taditarasamastavastuviṣayam ajñānādi vyāpakam, uta katipayagocaram iti vivecanīyam / na tāvad aśeṣaviṣayam, anupalabdheḥ / na khalu kumbhakāraḥ kumbhātireki kim api na vijānāti / atha katipayaviṣayam ? tad api na, aniyataviṣayatayā tasya tasya vyabhicāradarśanāt / na cāsti kiñcidvyavasthitam, yad avidyādimān eva kartṛtām anubhavati /
body.translated_text: As for the objection raised — that [our argument] proves the opposite of the intended <s>dharmaviśeṣa</s> (specific quality), since it would attribute limited power, knowledge, and lack of sovereignty — that is exceedingly crude, because those [limitations] are non-probative. For nothing that is being produced requires for its own origination the agent's incapacity or ignorance regarding other objects — since [effect-nature] merely implies a competent agent for its own accomplishment, and the pure negative concomitance [argument] is unestablished. Since the arising of the effect is accounted for by just that much [competence], it is impossible to posit as a cause the absence [of knowledge/power] regarding unrelated objects, [that absence] being entirely ineffective. Moreover, this must be examined: is that ignorance and the like regarding all other objects all-pervading, or limited to certain domains? It is certainly not all-encompassing, since that is unobserved. Surely the potter is not ignorant of everything other than pots. And is it limited to certain objects? That too is not [the case], because for each [agent], deviation is observed, since there is no fixed domain [of ignorance]. And there is nothing fixed such that only one who possesses ignorance and the like experiences agency.

children.text: yat tu parimita-śakti-jñāna-anaiśvarya-ādy-āpādanād dharma-viśeṣa-viparīta-sādhanatvam udbhāvitam, tad atisthavīyaḥ, aprayojakatvāt teṣām / na hi kiñcit kriyamāṇaṃ kartur artha-antara-viṣayam asāmarthyam ajñānaṃ vā sva-utpattaye 'pekṣate; sva-sampādana-samartha-kartṛ-mātra-ākṣepāt kevala-vyatireka-asiddheḥ / tāvata aiva upapadyamāne kārya-udaye sambandhino 'kiñcitkarasya artha-antara-viṣayasya abhāvasya hetutva-kalpanā-anupapatteḥ / api ca kiṃ tad-itara-samasta-vastu-viṣayam ajñāna-ādi vyāpakam, uta katipaya-gocaram iti vivecanīyam / na tāvad aśeṣa-viṣayam, anupalabdheḥ / na khalu kumbha-kāraḥ kumbha-atireki kim api na vijānāti / atha katipaya-viṣayam ? tad api na, aniyata-viṣayatayā tasya tasya vyabhicāra-darśanāt / na ca asti kiñcid-vyavasthitam, yad avidyā-ādimān eva kartṛtām anubhavati /

body.text: na ca śarīriṇaiva kartrā bhāvyam, śarīragrahaṇenaivānaikāntyāt / na khalu śarīraviśiṣṭas sann evāyam ātmā śarīram upādatte, ayogino yugapadanekaśarīragrahaṇāyogāt / pūrvadehaparityāgena dehāntaraprāpakakarmapreritaprāṇasahāya eva dehāntaraṃ praviśatīty upapāditam ātmacintāyām /
body.translated_text: Nor [is it valid to argue] that only an embodied being can be an agent, because [the argument based on] the qualifier 'having a body' alone is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntya</s>). For this Self does not take a body while already possessing a body — since for a non-yogin, the simultaneous grasping of multiple bodies is impossible. It has been established in the inquiry concerning the Self (<s>ātmacintā</s>) that [the Self], having abandoned the previous body, enters another body, assisted by the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) which is impelled by the <s>karma</s> that brings about [rebirth in] another body.

children.text: na ca śarīriṇa aiva kartrā bhāvyam, śarīra-grahaṇena eva anaikāntyāt / na khalu śarīra-viśiṣṭas sann eva ayam ātmā śarīram upādatte, ayogino yugapad-aneka-śarīra-grahaṇa-ayogāt / pūrva-deha-parityāgena deha-antara-prāpaka-karma-prerita-prāṇa-sahāya eva deha-antaraṃ praviśati ity upapāditam ātma-cintāyām /

body.text: kiñcid ātmā śarīram adhitiṣṭhato 'dhiṣṭhānakriyākarmabhūtasya dehasyādhiṣṭhātṛdaśa(deha?)anupraveśo 'nupapannaḥ, yugapad ekakriyāyām ekasya karmakartṛtvavirodhāt / adhitiṣṭhāsitadehasaṃyogavata eva tatpravṛttyanuguṇaprayatnayogalakṣaṇam adhiṣṭhānaṃ dṛṣṭam iti cet; astv ekatattva(stva)sambaddhasyādhiṣṭhānānupapatteḥ preryavastusambandhinā prerakeṇa bhavitavyam iti; na yato 'nyad apy adhiṣṭhīyamānaṃ mānadaṇḍādi svasambandhinaivādhiṣṭhīyate / tenādhiṣṭhānakriyāpekṣitādhiṣṭheyapadārthasambandhamātrātirekeṇa dehasambandho nāmāparo nādartavyaḥ / asti ceśvarasyāpi jagadupādānopakaraṇais sambandha ity uktam eva /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the entry of the <s>ātman</s> (self) — who governs the body — into the body, which is the object of the governing activity, is untenable, because of the contradiction in one [entity] being both the agent and the object of a single action simultaneously. If it be said that governance is observed to consist in the possession of effort conducive to the functioning of the body that is already conjoined with the body intended to be governed — let that be so; [but still,] since governance is untenable for [something] connected to a single entity, the impeller must be connected to the object to be impelled. For also [in ordinary experience], other things being governed — such as a measuring rod and the like — are governed only by one who is connected to them. Therefore, beyond the mere connection with the object to be governed that is required for the governing activity, no other connection called 'connection with a body' need be insisted upon. And it has already been stated that <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) too has a connection with the material causes and instruments of the world.

children.text: kiñcid ātmā śarīram adhitiṣṭhato 'dhiṣṭhāna-kriyā-karma-bhūtasya dehasya adhiṣṭhātṛ-daśa(deha?)-anupraveśo 'nupapannaḥ, yugapad eka-kriyāyām ekasya karma-kartṛtva-virodhāt / adhitiṣṭhāsita-deha-saṃyogavata eva tat-pravṛtty-anuguṇa-prayatna-yoga-lakṣaṇam adhiṣṭhānaṃ dṛṣṭam iti cet; astv eka-tattva(stva)-sambaddhasya adhiṣṭhāna-anupapatteḥ prerya-vastu-sambandhinā prerakeṇa bhavitavyam iti; na yato 'nyad apy adhiṣṭhīyamānaṃ māna-daṇḍa-ādi sva-sambandhina aiva adhiṣṭhīyate / tena adhiṣṭhāna-kriyā-apekṣita-adhiṣṭheya-pada-artha-sambandha-mātra-atirekeṇa deha-sambandho nāma aparo nā adartavyaḥ / asti cā iśvarasya api jagad-upādāna-upakaraṇais sambandha ity uktam eva /

body.text: atha svadehavyatirikte vastuni pravṛttiviśeṣakaratvaṃ dehadvāreṇaiva / dṛṣṭaṃ hi daṇḍacakrādiṣu karasaṃyogādinā kulālādeḥ pravartayitṛtvam ity ucyeta; tad api na; abhidhyānamātreṇaiva paraśarīragatagaranirasanac(v?)isāraṇadarśanāt / katham asati śarīre parapreraṇātmakaḥ saṅkalpa iti cet; kiṃ śarīraṃ saṅkalpayati, yena tadabhāve na bhavet ? / karaṇam iti cen na; manasaḥ karaṇatvāt / kim asatīśvarasya manaḥ ? bāḍham / nanv evaṃ vigrahadharmādharmānāśvaryādayaḥ sādhāraṇadharmāḥ prāduḥṣyuḥ / maivam; kāryatvākṣiptasamarthakartṛmattvād(ttvārtha?) draḍhimnaivāpāsatvāt / manaso nityendriyatayā dehāpagame 'pi sambandhābhyupagamād anaikāntikaś ca / yāvad dhi dṛṣṭānuguṇaṃ vyāptayupayogi, tāvad anujñāyate / na cāsmadāder manasāpy acintyaracanasyāparyantavistārasya mahābhūtabhautikaprapañcasya prādeśikaśarīrakaḥ kiñcijjñaḥ puṇyapāpaparavaśagatir alaṃ nirmāṇāyety aparimitajñānāiśvaryaśaktiḥ śarīrādyanapekṣaḥ saṅkalpād eva sakalabhuvananirmāṇakṣamaḥ kartā siddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, [if it be objected that] the capacity to cause specific activity in objects other than one's own body is only through the medium of a body — for it is observed that a potter and the like cause movement in a staff, wheel, and such things through the conjunction of the hand and so on — to that also [we say]: no; because it is seen that one can expel and remove poison located in another's body through mere willing (<s>abhidhyāna</s>). If [it be objected:] how can there be a volition whose nature is the impulsion of others without a body? — [we reply:] does the body produce the volition, such that in its absence there would be none? If [you say] it is the instrument — no, because the mind (<s>manas</s>) is the instrument. Is <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) then without a mind? Certainly not. But then [you may object that] attributes common [to embodied beings] such as having a body, <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), non-lordship, and the like would arise [for the Lord]. Not so; because [these are] set aside firmly by the fact that being an effect necessitates a competent maker. And [the argument] is also inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because the mind, being an eternal sense organ, is admitted to have connection [with the self] even when the body has perished. For only as much as is useful for establishing invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) in accordance with observation is admitted. And one who is a partial-knowing being (<s>kiñcijjña</s>), confined to a limited body, subject to the control of <s>puṇya</s> (merit) and <s>pāpa</s> (demerit), like ourselves, is certainly not capable of constructing this world of inconceivable design and boundless extent, [comprising] the manifold array of gross elements and their derivatives — therefore a maker is established who possesses unlimited knowledge, lordship, and power, who is independent of body and the like, and who is capable of constructing all worlds by mere volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) alone.

children.text: atha sva-deha-vyatirikte vastuni pravṛtti-viśeṣa-karatvaṃ deha-dvāreṇa eva / dṛṣṭaṃ hi daṇḍa-cakra-ādiṣu kara-saṃyoga-ādinā kulāla-ādeḥ pravartayitṛtvam ity ucyeta; tad api na; abhidhyāna-mātreṇa eva para-śarīra-gata-gara-nirasana-c(v?)isāraṇa-darśanāt / katham asati śarīre para-preraṇa-ātmakaḥ saṅkalpa iti cet; kiṃ śarīraṃ saṅkalpayati, yena tad-abhāve na bhavet ? / karaṇam iti cen na; manasaḥ karaṇatvāt / kim asatī iśvarasya manaḥ ? bāḍham / nanv evaṃ vigraha-dharma-adharma-anāśvarya-ādayaḥ sādhāraṇa-dharmāḥ prāduḥṣyuḥ / ma aivam; kāryatva-ākṣipta-samartha-kartṛmattvād(-ttva-artha?) draḍhimna aiva apāsatvāt / manaso nitya-indriyatayā deha-apagame 'pi sambandha-abhyupagamād anaikāntikaś ca / yāvad dhi dṛṣṭa-anuguṇaṃ vyāptay-upayogi, tāvad anujñāyate / na ca asmad-āder manasa āpy acintya-racanasya aparyanta-vistārasya mahābhūta-bhautika-prapañcasya prādeśika-śarīrakaḥ kiñcij-jñaḥ puṇya-pāpa-paravaśa-gatir alaṃ nirmāṇāya ity aparimita-jñāna-aiśvarya-śaktiḥ śarīra-ādy-anapekṣaḥ saṅkalpād eva sakala-bhuvana-nirmāṇa-kṣamaḥ kartā siddhaḥ /

body.text: īdṛśena kartrā ghaṭādiṣu kāryatvasya sambandho na dṛṣṭa iti cet; atigahanagiritaṭādhiṣṭhānenātiprakṛṣṭādṛṣṭacarendhananivahasambandhinā hutavahaviśeṣeṇa mahānasādau dhūmasya vā kiṃ sambandho dṛṣṭaḥ ? yena dhūmaviśeṣadarśanād giriśikhare tathāvidhāgnir anumīyate / yādṛśo dhūmo yatrāvagataḥ tatraiva tādṛśas tatsampādanasamartho dṛṣtāntabhūmāv aparidṛṣṭo 'pi sāmānyavyāptibalena pakṣadharmatāvaśāt sidhyatīti cet; tad idam asmābhir abhidhīyamānaṃ kim iti na hṛdayam adhirohati bhavatām / ihāpi kāryatvaṃ samarthakartṛpūrvakatvena ghaṭādiṣu viditasambandhaniyamaṃ kṣtityādiṣu dṛśyamānaṃ svasampādanasamartham adṛṣṭapūrvam eva buddhimatkartāram upasthāpayati / yathaiva hi deśakālendhanaparimāṇādiviśeṣānādareṇa dhūmasya svodayānuguṇahutavahamātreṇa sambandhaniyamaḥ, tathaivānīśvaratvākiñcijjñatvaśarīritvapuṇyapāpaparavaśatvam anuṣyatvādiviśeṣaprahāṇena kāryasya svanirmāṇasamarthabuddhimatkartṛmātreṇa sambandhaniyamaniścaya iti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: If [it be objected that] a connection of such a maker with the property of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) in pots and the like is not observed — [we reply:] has any connection been observed between the smoke in a kitchen and a particular fire associated with a heap of fuel that is exceedingly remote and never seen, situated on the slope of an extremely dense mountain? — by which [connection] a fire of that kind is inferred on a mountain peak from the observation of a particular [kind of] smoke. If [you say:] the kind of smoke that has been ascertained in a particular location — even though a [fire] of that kind, capable of producing it, has not been observed in the exemplary domain — is established by the force of the general invariable concomitance (<s>sāmānyavyāpti</s>) and by virtue of [its] being a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) — then why does this very [principle] that we are stating not enter your hearts? Here too, the property of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>), whose invariable connection with a competent maker is known in [the case of] pots and the like, when observed in the earth and the rest, presents an intelligent maker capable of producing it — one that has never been seen before. For just as smoke has an invariable connection merely with a fire conducive to its own arising, regardless of specific differences in location, time, quantity of fuel, and the like — in exactly the same way, the property of being an effect has a determined invariable connection merely with an intelligent maker competent for its own production, setting aside particular attributes such as non-lordship, limited knowledge, embodiment, subjection to <s>puṇya</s> (merit) and <s>pāpa</s> (demerit), and mortality — therefore there is no distinction [between the two cases].

children.text: īdṛśena kartrā ghaṭa-ādiṣu kāryatvasya sambandho na dṛṣṭa iti cet; atigahana-giri-taṭa-adhiṣṭhānena atiprakṛṣṭa-adṛṣṭa-cara-indhana-nivaha-sambandhinā hutavaha-viśeṣeṇa mahānasa-ādau dhūmasya vā kiṃ sambandho dṛṣṭaḥ ? yena dhūma-viśeṣa-darśanād giri-śikhare tathā-vidha-agnir anumīyate / yādṛśo dhūmo yatra avagataḥ tatra eva tādṛśas tat-sampādana-samartho dṛṣtānta-bhūmāv aparidṛṣṭo 'pi sāmānya-vyāpti-balena pakṣa-dharmatā-vaśāt sidhyati iti cet; tad idam asmābhir abhidhīyamānaṃ kim iti na hṛdayam adhirohati bhavatām / iha api kāryatvaṃ samartha-kartṛ-pūrvakatvena ghaṭa-ādiṣu vidita-sambandha-niyamaṃ kṣtity-ādiṣu dṛśyamānaṃ sva-sampādana-samartham adṛṣṭa-pūrvam eva buddhimat-kartāram upasthāpayati / yatha aiva hi deśa-kāla-indhana-parimāṇa-ādi-viśeṣa-anādareṇa dhūmasya sva-udaya-anuguṇa-hutavaha-mātreṇa sambandha-niyamaḥ, tatha aiva anīśvaratva-akiñcij-jñatva-śarīritva-puṇya-pāpa-para-vaśatvam anuṣyatva-ādi-viśeṣa-prahāṇena kāryasya sva-nirmāṇa-samartha-buddhimat-kartṛ-mātreṇa sambandha-niyama-niścaya iti na kaścid-viśeṣaḥ /

body.text: api ca vibhudravyasaṃyoginaḥ parispandavataś ca sarvatra sparśavattvāvyabhicāre 'pi jñānasukhādinityadravyaviśeṣaguṇānumitātmasaṃyogino manasaḥ katham iva sparśarahitatatvam ? kathaṃ ca vāyavīyadravyasya mahimaguṇaśālino niyatādhiṣṭhānasparśanatvaniyamadarśane 'pi tvagindriye tadviparyayaḥ ? taijasasya vā rūpasparśayor anyattarasya vā prākaṭyaniyame 'pi rūpopalambhasādhanatānumitataijasabhāvasya cakṣuṣo niyamena tadubhayānudbhavābhyupagamaḥ ? / atha kāryadarśanānumitasadbhāvānāṃ taijasādibhāve 'pi tattadviśeṣaṇāṃ yogyānupalabdhibādhitatvāt tadabhyupagame 'nekaniyamabhaṅgaprasaṅgāc ca tathābhyupagamaḥ, hanta tarhi prakṛtaviṣaye 'pi prasañjitadharmaviśeṣāṇām anupalambhabādhāviśeṣād anekaniyamadarśanavighātaprasaṅgāc ca tathābhyupagama iti sarvaṃ samānam anyatrābhiniveśāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, even when there is no deviation from the rule that everything conjoined with a substance possessing the universal [quality] and possessing vibration is always endowed with touch — how can the mind (<s>manas</s>), which is conjoined with the self (inferred by the special qualities of eternal substances such as knowledge, pleasure, etc.) and which possesses vibration, be devoid of touch? And how, when one observes the rule that the aerial substance (<s>vāyu</s>), which possesses the quality of greatness (<s>mahiman</s>), invariably manifests touch at its established substratum — can there be the opposite [i.e., no touch] in the case of the tactile sense-organ? Or for the fiery [substance], even though the rule is that [only] one of form and touch is manifest, how can one accept the invariable non-manifestation of both in the eye, whose fiery nature is inferred as the means of apprehending form? If it be [argued that] even though the fiery nature etc. is established by inference from the perception of effects, since the particular properties [ascribed to them] are contradicted by the non-perception of what is fit to be perceived (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>), and since accepting those [properties] would lead to the unwanted consequence of breaking many established rules — therefore such acceptance [is justified]; well then, in the matter at hand too, since the particular properties attributed [to the inferred cause] are no differently contradicted by non-perception, and since there would be the equal consequence of breaking many rules — therefore such acceptance is equally justified. Everything is the same [in both cases], except for [the opponent's] prejudice.

children.text: api ca vibhu-dravya-saṃyoginaḥ parispandavataś ca sarvatra sparśavattva-avyabhicāre 'pi jñāna-sukha-ādi-nitya-dravya-viśeṣa-guṇa-anumita-ātma-saṃyogino manasaḥ katham iva sparśa-rahitatatvam ? kathaṃ ca vāyavīya-dravyasya mahima-guṇa-śālino niyata-adhiṣṭhāna-sparśanatva-niyama-darśane 'pi tvag-indriye tad-viparyayaḥ ? taijasasya vā rūpa-sparśayor anyattarasya vā prākaṭya-niyame 'pi rūpa-upalambha-sādhanata ānumita-taijasa-bhāvasya cakṣuṣo niyamena tad-ubhaya-anudbhava-abhyupagamaḥ ? / atha kārya-darśana-anumita-sad-bhāvānāṃ taijasa-ādi-bhāve 'pi tat-tad-viśeṣaṇāṃ yogya-anupalabdhi-bādhitatvāt tad-abhyupagame 'neka-niyama-bhaṅga-prasaṅgāc ca tatha ābhyupagamaḥ, hanta tarhi prakṛta-viṣaye 'pi prasañjita-dharma-viśeṣāṇām anupalambha-bādhā-viśeṣād aneka-niyama-darśana-vighāta-prasaṅgāc ca tatha ābhyupagama iti sarvaṃ samānam anyatra abhiniveśāt /

body.text: dṛśyante hi nītayaḥ / yathā vivādāspadaṃ paramāṇvādi prekṣāvatpreritaṃ ceṣṭate, acetanatvāt; yad acetanaṃ tat tathā, yathā tathāvidhaṃ kandukādi / tathā vivādādhyāsitā bāhyābhyantarapravṛttayaḥ prakṛtyupakaraṇapratyakṣapūrvikāḥ kāryatvāt tadvad eva |
body.translated_text: Observe the following logical arguments (<s>nīti</s>): The disputed atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) and such act [purposefully] when impelled by an intelligent being, because they are non-conscious (<s>acetana</s>); whatever is non-conscious acts thus, like a ball and such of that kind. Similarly, the disputed external and internal activities [of the world] are preceded by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) of the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) and instruments (<s>upakaraṇa</s>), because they are effects (<s>kārya</s>) — just like those [pots, etc.].

children.text: dṛśyante hi nītayaḥ / yathā vivāda-āspadaṃ parama-aṇv-ādi prekṣāvat-preritaṃ ca iṣṭate, acetanatvāt; yad acetanaṃ tat tathā, yathā tathā-vidhaṃ kanduka-ādi / tathā vivāda-adhyāsitā bāhya-abhyantara-pravṛttayaḥ prakṛty-upa-karaṇa-pratyakṣa-pūrvikāḥ kāryatvāt tadvad eva |

children.translated_text: That [God] is directly perceivable (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), because He is a knowable object (<s>prameya</s>), because He is a real entity (<s>padārtha</s>) — like a pot and such.
This [world] conforms to the will of a single [being], because it is non-conscious (<s>acaitanya</s>) — like one's own body.
All conscious beings perform their effects under the superintendence of one [being],
because their production of effects depends on a connection with a body — like the tactile sense-organ (<s>tvak</s>) and such.
The disputed world has a single supreme person (<s>puruṣa</s>) as its principal,
because it consists of both conscious and non-conscious [entities] — like a country with a single king.
